r3picks.text:
My pick per direction

02 Ember tile → 02b List mark. It's literally the app's list mark (20×16, radius 4 of 20, the same finish) with a check: the most "this app" of the four, and the plain body around it keeps it from being one more orange square. 02a is louder in the Dock, if you want loud.

03 Fan → 03b Tight. Round 2's fan goes to mush at 16; bigger tiles at half the angle, parted by a gap, still read as a stack. 03c (Today on top) is the nicer idea, but the sun turns to a speck below 32.

01 Spark → 01b Lit round. The app's checked box is round, so this is the app's own mark, and it no longer looks like 02b (01a and 02b are nearly the same icon).

10 Tick → 10a Refined, flat. The two-tone check is the idea; lighting it either loses the two tones (10b) or turns it into 02a with a tick (10c).

If I had to pick one overall: 02b.

r3how.text:
What "lit" copies, and from where

app/TasksCore/Sources/TasksTheme/TileArt.swift (TileArt.draw), the finish of every list mark, which is design/COLOR.md §2's reading of docs/feedback/reference-tile.svg:

• Fill: the flat hue. Ember #E6683D; the fan's back tiles use the app's own tile hues, magenta #6B4FB8 and cyan #146E77 (Theme.rex).
• Light: radial from the top middle, radii 1.4 × width and 1.1 × height. White 0.216 × (1 − s(d/0.58)) to 0.58, then black 0.072 × s((d − 0.58)/0.42), smootherstep, at the source's 15 stops.
• Specular: a strip along the top edge, white, peaking mid-width.
• Ring: white 10%, just inside the edge.
• Halo: black just outside the edge, 35% in dark and 18% in light (tileHalo).
• Glyphs: white and flat.

Scale: the app snaps the strip, ring and halo to one device pixel, because at 20pt they fall under a pixel. The icon draws them at the source's own size instead (one unit is 1/45.54 of the tile's height), at the source's alphas (strip peak 36%, ring 10%). Round marks skip the strip, as TileArt does for the brand mark's head.

weak.text:
What might be weak about the current icon (guesses for you to confirm, not your reasons)

1. It's off-palette. The app went Ember on 2026-11-01, but the icon's head is still Rex blue (#2F81F7).

2. Its idea doesn't show. The sync log drawn as a commit graph is an engineer's in-joke; to anyone else it's a bulleted checklist, the most common to-do glyph there is.

3. It's weak at small sizes. At 16 and 32 it's a blue dot beside grey dashes, with no silhouette of its own in the Dock or a Finder list.

4. It doesn't share the app's finish. The app now draws solid, lit tiles with white glyphs; the icon is a flat diagram of thin parts.

5. It's busy: nine parts (three nodes, two links, three bars and a check) for an app whose point is quiet.

top3.text:
My top 3

1. 05 t. The only one that's a name and not a checkbox: an ownable letterform, with the Ember crossbar as a task row. It reads at 16 and sits apart in the Dock. The risk is that it ties the icon to the working name "Tasks".

2. 06 Breakout. A single gesture, a check leaving its ring (done, and moving on). It has a clear round silhouette at 16, and the two colours separate the two strokes. The risk is that it's in the check-circle family.

3. 01 Spark. It uses what the app already does: the Ember checkbox and the spark it plays when you finish a task (COLOR.md D). It's the warmest and most "this app" of the set. At 16 the rays thin to a halo, but the orange square still carries it.

Safe fallback: 02 Ember tile is the strongest at 16, but also the most generic.
